es: Reconocer cómo se describen el método y la muestra de un estudio con el pasivo en pasado (was conducted, participants were recruited) y valorar qué revela cada decisión metodológica.

teaching.en: The survey was conducted online over six weeks, and the response rate, barely a quarter, limits what the authors can claim.
teaching.es: La encuesta se realizó en línea durante seis semanas, y la tasa de respuesta, apenas una cuarta parte, limita lo que los autores pueden afirmar.
teaching.explanationEs: El pasivo sin agente (was conducted) centra la frase en el procedimiento; la tasa de respuesta dice cuánta gente contestó.
segments: The survey was conducted online over six weeks, and the response
rate, barely a quarter, limits what the authors can claim.
teaching.audioText: The survey was conducted online over six weeks, and the response rate, barely a quarter, limits what the authors can claim.

teaching.en: Participants were recruited through local clubs, which is why the authors hesitate to call it a representative sample.
teaching.es: Los participantes fueron captados a través de clubes locales, por eso los autores dudan en llamarla una muestra representativa.
teaching.explanationEs: Recruited describe cómo se consiguió a la gente; ese método condiciona si la muestra representa a toda la población.
segments: Participants were recruited through local clubs, which is why
the authors hesitate to call it a representative sample.
teaching.audioText: Participants were recruited through local clubs, which is why the authors hesitate to call it a representative sample.

teaching.en: Two hundred participants were randomly selected from the council's list, so every name had an equal chance of being chosen.
teaching.es: Doscientos participantes fueron elegidos por sorteo de la lista municipal, así que cada nombre tenía la misma probabilidad de salir.
teaching.explanationEs: Randomly selected indica que la elección no dependió de nadie: es la mejor defensa contra el sesgo de selección.
segments: Two hundred participants were randomly selected from the council's list,
so every name had an equal chance of being chosen.
teaching.audioText: Two hundred participants were randomly selected from the council's list, so every name had an equal chance of being chosen.

teaching.en: Everyone interviewed had given informed consent beforehand, and each conversation was recorded and transcribed word for word.
teaching.es: Todos los entrevistados habían dado su consentimiento informado de antemano, y cada conversación se grabó y se transcribió palabra por palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Had given (pasado perfecto) marca lo que ocurrió antes de la entrevista; informed consent es una garantía ética.
segments: Everyone interviewed had given informed consent beforehand, and each
conversation was recorded and transcribed word for word.
teaching.audioText: Everyone interviewed had given informed consent beforehand, and each conversation was recorded and transcribed word for word.

teaching.en: A short questionnaire was also posted to households picked at random, to reach people who avoid answering the phone.
teaching.es: También se envió por correo un breve cuestionario a hogares elegidos al azar, para llegar a quienes evitan contestar el teléfono.
teaching.explanationEs: At random = sin criterio propio; to reach… explica el propósito de un paso del método.
segments: A short questionnaire was also posted to households picked at
random, to reach people who avoid answering the phone.
teaching.audioText: A short questionnaire was also posted to households picked at random, to reach people who avoid answering the phone.

teaching.en: Notice what the passive leaves out: the report never says who conducted the survey, and that silence can matter.
teaching.es: Fíjate en lo que el pasivo omite: el informe nunca dice quién realizó la encuesta, y ese silencio puede importar.
teaching.explanationEs: El pasivo sin agente es cómodo, pero un lector crítico se pregunta quién hizo cada paso.
segments: Notice what the passive leaves out: the report never says
who conducted the survey, and that silence can matter.
teaching.audioText: Notice what the passive leaves out: the report never says who conducted the survey, and that silence can matter.

prompt.es: Según el método, ¿qué limita más la representatividad de la muestra?

choices.text: The group was built from people already linked to one gym.
The interviews were held one week after the first replies arrived.
Only two hundred people were interviewed in the whole study.

feedback.es: Reclutar desde la página de un gimnasio sesga la muestra hacia gente ya activa; el plazo y la cifra no son el problema principal.

hint.es: Piensa en quién sigue la página de un gimnasio.

origin.text: Method. Participants were recruited through the social media page of a local gym, and the first two hundred people who replied were interviewed the following week.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los participantes fueron elegidos al azar de una lista municipal.»

feedback.es: Selected at random describe una elección sin criterio personal, que protege el estudio contra el sesgo de selección.

hint.es: Dos palabras: significa sin ningún orden ni preferencia.

origin.text: To avoid any bias, the participants were selected ___ from the council's list; nobody chose them by hand, and every name had the same chance.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de un método con el paso que describe.

pairs: Volunteers were recruited through a local radio station.
Everyone signed a consent form before the interview.
Each conversation was recorded and then transcribed.
The data were analysed by two researchers working independently.

feedback.es: Cada verbo en pasivo señala un paso distinto: captar, proteger con el consentimiento, guardar las entrevistas y analizar los datos.

hint.es: Mira el verbo en pasivo de cada frase: indica qué se hizo en ese paso.

pairs: Volunteers were recruited through a local radio station.
Everyone signed a consent form before the interview.
Each conversation was recorded and then transcribed.
The data were analysed by two researchers working independently.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestran los autores ante la baja tasa de respuesta?

choices.text: They regret the low rate and treat the findings as unreliable.
They admit a weakness but argue that the results still hold.
They accept the flaw and say the rate was typical of such surveys.

feedback.es: Reconocen la debilidad («we accept») pero se apoyan en que el patrón se repite en las dos rondas; ni la minimizan del todo, ni la consideran fatal, ni citan datos comparativos.

origin.text: The response rate was 23 per cent. We would have liked it to be higher, and we accept that those who replied may differ from those who did not; even so, the pattern was the same in both rounds.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué tienen en común el sorteo de nombres y la lectura de los diarios.

choices.text: Both give every pupil the same amount of time to write.
Both make sure each school contributes diaries of equal length.
Both stop the researchers' own preferences from shaping the data.

feedback.es: Sortear nombres y hacer que los diarios los lea gente que no conocía a los alumnos cumplen la misma función: que las preferencias o el conocimiento personal de los investigadores no influyan en los datos.

origin.audio: Researchers visited twelve schools last spring. In each school, ten pupils were picked by drawing names from a hat, and every one of them was asked to keep a diary for a week. The diaries were collected on Friday and read by two people who had never met the pupils.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Se obtuvo el consentimiento informado antes de grabar cualquier entrevista.»

answer.text: Informed consent was obtained before any interview was recorded
accepted: Informed consent was obtained before any interview was recorded
Before any interview was recorded informed consent was obtained

feedback.es: La estructura sujeto + was obtained + before + sujeto + was recorded une dos pasivos en pasado y marca cuál ocurrió primero.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la última frase del fragmento sobre los resultados?

choices.text: The results may make local feeling appear stronger than it really is.
They probably make local feeling look weaker, since people with mild views did not reply.
They cast doubt on the figures only for the households contacted by post.

feedback.es: Si contestan sobre todo quienes tienen opiniones fuertes, el resultado puede exagerar la intensidad del sentir local; no lo subestima, ni afecta solo a la segunda ronda, ni lo prueba.

origin.text: Method. The survey was conducted between March and May. A letter was sent to 1,200 households chosen at random from the council's register, and adults were invited to complete the questionnaire online. Only 312 replied, a response rate of 26 per cent, so a further 400 households were contacted by post. Nobody was paid, but everyone was told that the findings would be shared with the council. All answers were recorded anonymously, and both rounds were combined before analysis. The authors admit that people with strong opinions may have been more likely to reply.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué se dejó fuera al grupo piloto de las cifras finales.

choices.text: Their replies were lost when the questionnaire was revised.
Having already read the first version, they might answer differently.
Twenty volunteers were too few to make any difference to the totals.

feedback.es: Sara explica que los voluntarios ya conocían la redacción original, así que sus respuestas podían no ser comparables con las del resto.

origin.audio: At Tuesday's meeting, Sara summarised the method for her colleagues. The questionnaire had been piloted with twenty volunteers, then changed after several of them said that question seven was confusing. Only then was it sent to the main sample. Leo asked why the pilot group was not counted in the final figures, and Sara replied that, having already seen the original wording, those volunteers could have answered differently from everyone else.

prompt.es: Completa: «Solo entonces dieron su consentimiento informado.»

feedback.es: Informed consent es la colocación fija: aceptar participar tras recibir toda la información.

origin.text: Before the first question, each person was told what the study was for and that they could stop at any time. Only then did they give informed ___.

prompt.es: Empareja cada frase del informe con lo que aporta al lector.

pairs: Forty adults were contacted by post.

pairs.es: Cómo se llegó a la gente

pairs: Names were drawn from a hat.

pairs.es: Por qué la elección es imparcial

pairs: Nobody was paid to take part.
Replies were kept without names.
The pilot group was left out.

feedback.es: Cada frase revela un aspecto distinto del método: el contacto, la imparcialidad, los incentivos, la privacidad y la corrección de sesgos.

pairs: Forty adults were contacted by post.

pairs.es: Cómo se llegó a la gente

pairs: Names were drawn from a hat.

pairs.es: Por qué la elección es imparcial

pairs: Nobody was paid to take part.
Replies were kept without names.
The pilot group was left out.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende señalar el autor con este párrafo?

choices.text: That the passive makes the report harder to read than the active would.
That one person alone probably did all three steps.
That the passive hides who was responsible, so readers cannot judge the work.

feedback.es: El autor señala que el pasivo oculta quién hizo cada paso; no critica la legibilidad y solo plantea la duda de si una misma persona hizo las tres tareas, no la da por cierta.

origin.text: The interviews were conducted, the recordings were transcribed and the main themes were identified. Nowhere does the report say who did any of this, or whether one person did all three.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La muestra se eligió al azar, pero solo respondió una cuarta parte.»

answer.text: The sample was selected at random but only a quarter replied
accepted: The sample was selected at random but only a quarter replied
Only a quarter replied but the sample was selected at random

feedback.es: Was selected at random describe el método y but only a quarter replied revela el límite, en el orden natural del informe.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el horario de las llamadas sobre quién respondió.

choices.text: Those at home during working hours were more likely to be reached.
Office workers were the group most likely to be reached.
Households with young children were always called first.

feedback.es: Llamar solo en horario laboral favorece a quienes están en casa a esas horas, así que la muestra puede quedar desequilibrada.

origin.audio: The survey was conducted by telephone, and all the calls were made between nine and five on weekdays.

es: Describir datos con proporciones y comparaciones precisas (the vast majority, a sizeable minority, just under a third, twice as many, account for, outnumber) y leer con sentido crítico lo que una cifra sugiere.

teaching.en: Roughly a third of the residents, 34 per cent, use the bus daily, yet the vast majority, 91 per cent, own a bicycle.
teaching.es: Aproximadamente un tercio de los vecinos, el 34 por ciento, usa el autobús a diario, pero la gran mayoría, el 91 por ciento, tiene una bicicleta.
teaching.explanationEs: Roughly suaviza la cifra; the vast majority equivale a «casi todos»; per cent no lleva -s.
segments: Roughly a third of the residents, 34 per cent, use the bus
daily, yet the vast majority, 91 per cent, own a bicycle.
teaching.audioText: Roughly a third of the residents, 34 per cent, use the bus daily, yet the vast majority, 91 per cent, own a bicycle.

teaching.en: Cyclists now outnumber train passengers: twice as many residents cycle as take the train, although a sizeable minority still drive.
teaching.es: Los ciclistas ya superan en número a los pasajeros del tren: el doble de vecinos usa la bicicleta que el tren, aunque una minoría considerable sigue conduciendo.
teaching.explanationEs: Outnumber es transitivo (outnumber someone, sin preposición); twice as many… as compara dos cantidades contables.
segments: Cyclists now outnumber train passengers: twice as many residents cycle
as take the train, although a sizeable minority still drive.
teaching.audioText: Cyclists now outnumber train passengers: twice as many residents cycle as take the train, although a sizeable minority still drive.

teaching.en: A negligible proportion, barely two per cent, arrive by taxi, so the council can safely ignore that figure.
teaching.es: Una proporción insignificante, apenas el dos por ciento, llega en taxi, así que el municipio puede ignorar esa cifra sin riesgo.
teaching.explanationEs: Barely y a negligible proportion subrayan que una cantidad es tan pequeña que casi no cuenta.
segments: A negligible proportion, barely two per cent, arrive by
taxi, so the council can safely ignore that figure.
teaching.audioText: A negligible proportion, barely two per cent, arrive by taxi, so the council can safely ignore that figure.

teaching.en: Car use rose slightly, from just under a fifth of journeys to just over a fifth, which is hardly a trend.
teaching.es: El uso del auto subió ligeramente, de un poco menos de un quinto de los viajes a un poco más de un quinto, lo que difícilmente es una tendencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Just under / just over sitúan la cifra respecto a una fracción redonda; slightly acompaña cambios pequeños.
segments: Car use rose slightly, from just under a fifth of journeys
to just over a fifth, which is hardly a trend.
teaching.audioText: Car use rose slightly, from just under a fifth of journeys to just over a fifth, which is hardly a trend.

teaching.en: Students account for roughly half of all cyclists, so any change to the cycle lanes will affect them most.
teaching.es: Los estudiantes representan aproximadamente la mitad de todos los ciclistas, así que cualquier cambio en los carriles bici les afectará más.
teaching.explanationEs: Account for + porcentaje indica qué parte del total supone un grupo; no se traduce como «dar cuenta de».
segments: Students account for roughly half of all cyclists, so any
change to the cycle lanes will affect them most.
teaching.audioText: Students account for roughly half of all cyclists, so any change to the cycle lanes will affect them most.

prompt.es: Elige la expresión que describe fielmente el dato del gráfico.

choices.text: a sizeable minority of the students
a negligible proportion of the students
the vast majority of the students

feedback.es: Siete de doscientos es una cantidad tan pequeña que casi no cuenta: a negligible proportion.

hint.es: Fíjate en que 3,5 por ciento es una cifra muy baja.

origin.text: Chart: of 200 students, 7 arrive by taxi, which is 3.5 per cent of the group.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los estudiantes representan aproximadamente la mitad de los ciclistas.»

feedback.es: Account for + porcentaje expresa qué parte del total supone un grupo.

hint.es: El verbo va seguido de for y significa «representar una parte».

origin.text: Figures from the cycle scheme show that students ___ for roughly half of all cyclists; staff make up most of the rest.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con el porcentaje al que suele corresponder.

pairs: the vast majority
just under half
a sizeable minority
a negligible proportion

feedback.es: Cada expresión cubre una franja distinta: casi todos, casi la mitad, una parte notable y casi nada.

hint.es: Ordénalas mentalmente de la mayor a la menor proporción.

pairs: the vast majority
just under half
a sizeable minority
a negligible proportion

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué advierten los autores sobre el aumento del ciclismo.

choices.text: That cycling is growing too slowly to matter to the council.
That the fall in car use is the real story here.
That the growth is striking, but the numbers involved remain very small.

feedback.es: Los autores piden cautela: duplicar un dato muy pequeño llama la atención, pero los conductores siguen siendo diez veces más; ni restan importancia al ciclismo ni ven en la bajada del auto la noticia.

origin.audio: The council's latest figures show that car journeys have fallen slightly, from 41 to 40 per cent, whereas cycling has doubled, from two to four per cent. Even so, drivers still outnumber cyclists ten to one, and the authors warn against reading too much into a change this small.

prompt.es: Completa: «La proporción de conductores bajó ligeramente este año.»

feedback.es: Un punto porcentual es un cambio pequeño: slightly acompaña verbos como fell o rose.

origin.text: The proportion of people who drive fell ___ this year, from 41 to 40 per cent, a change too small to be called a trend.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe fielmente los datos.

choices.text: Walkers account for just under half of the pupils.
Cyclists account for roughly a third of the pupils.
Bus users outnumber cyclists by a wide margin.

feedback.es: 245 de 500 es un poco menos de la mitad; los ciclistas son una cuarta parte y los usuarios del autobús no superan a los ciclistas.

origin.text: Survey of 500 pupils: 245 walk, 130 cycle and 125 take the bus.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere el informe sobre la petición de un estacionamiento nuevo?

choices.text: It reflects the wishes of the drivers, who are the largest group.
It is a minor concern for staff compared with bicycle storage.
It matters more to drivers who live close to the site.

feedback.es: Solo una proporción insignificante lo pidió, mientras que casi todos los menores de treinta pidieron guardabicicletas; además, los conductores (360 de 1.200) no son el grupo mayoritario.

origin.text: Commuting report. The survey was sent to every member of staff, and replies came back from all three sites. Of the 1,200 employees who answered, 780 use public transport, 360 drive and 60 cycle. Among the drivers, just over half live within ten kilometres of the site, so a tram stop would suit them. Cyclists are barely five per cent of the total, yet nearly everyone under thirty asked for secure bicycle storage. Women account for roughly 58 per cent of respondents but only a third of the drivers. Only a negligible proportion of staff asked for a new car park, although several admitted that they seldom use the present one.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las mujeres superan en número a los hombres en doscientas personas.»

feedback.es: Outnumber es un verbo transitivo: se construye sin preposición y significa ser más numerosos que otro grupo.

origin.text: Of the 1,200 respondents, 700 were women and 500 were men, so women ___ men by two hundred.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué Mia menciona que solo contestaron cincuenta personas.

choices.text: She suspected the survey had been sent to the wrong staff.
She thought forty per cent was too low to be worth reporting.
The percentage sounded much bigger than the small numbers justified.

feedback.es: Mia señala que un cuarenta por ciento son solo veinte personas: el porcentaje suena más grande de lo que justifican los números.

origin.audio: In Monday's meeting, Tom presented the figures from the staff survey. Forty per cent of employees, he said, were unhappy with the parking, but when Mia looked at the table she noticed that only fifty people had answered, so forty per cent meant twenty people. Tom agreed that a percentage can sound dramatic when the sample is small, and he promised to add the real numbers to the report.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aproximadamente dos tercios de los encuestados viven a menos de diez minutos.»

answer.text: Roughly two thirds of the respondents live within ten minutes

feedback.es: Roughly suaviza la fracción y within ten minutes cierra el dato con la distancia.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura adopta el autor ante el verbo «surged»?

choices.text: He finds it too dramatic for such small numbers.
He thinks it plays down a real and striking rise.
He uses it because the percentage has doubled.

feedback.es: El autor reconoce que el dato se duplicó, pero considera que el verbo exagera lo que los números pequeños permiten afirmar.

origin.text: Headline writers love dramatic verbs. A rise from two to four per cent is a doubling, yet it still describes only a small share of the population, and to say that cycling has surged is to let the verb do the work that the numbers have not earned.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ese 29 % queda un poco por debajo de un tercio.»

feedback.es: Just under sitúa la cifra justo por debajo de una fracción redonda: 29 es un poco menos de un tercio.

origin.text: In the vote, 29 per cent of residents took part. That is ___ a third, so nobody can claim that the neighbourhood as a whole has spoken.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué implica la precaución de los autores.

choices.text: Most pupils are afraid of cycling near the school.
Safety may look better than other pupils would report.
Three quarters of all pupils cycle to school.

feedback.es: Como solo respondieron quienes ya van en bicicleta, el dato puede hacer que la seguridad parezca mayor de lo que dirían los demás.

origin.audio: Three out of four pupils who answered said that they felt safe cycling to school. But the survey was sent only to pupils who already cycle, so the authors caution that the figure tells us little about everyone else.

title.en: What the data can and cannot show
title.es: Lo que los datos pueden y no pueden demostrar

es: Distinguir lo que un estudio demuestra de lo que solo sugiere, detectar sus límites (muestra, datos autodeclarados, factores ocultos) y juzgar qué conclusiones están justificadas al escuchar o leer una reseña.

teaching.en: The study suggests that teenagers who sleep longer score higher, yet the authors stop short of claiming a causal link.
teaching.es: El estudio sugiere que los adolescentes que duermen más sacan mejores notas, pero los autores no llegan a afirmar una relación causal.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggests es un verbo cauto: apunta a una relación; stop short of + -ing marca que los autores no dan el paso siguiente.
segments: The study suggests that teenagers who sleep longer score higher,
yet the authors stop short of claiming a causal link.
teaching.audioText: The study suggests that teenagers who sleep longer score higher, yet the authors stop short of claiming a causal link.

teaching.en: A strong correlation does not demonstrate that one thing causes another, because a third factor may explain both.
teaching.es: Una correlación fuerte no demuestra que una cosa cause la otra, porque un tercer factor puede explicar ambas.
teaching.explanationEs: Demonstrate es un verbo fuerte que exige pruebas de causa; una correlación solo muestra que dos datos van juntos.
segments: A strong correlation does not demonstrate that one thing
causes another, because a third factor may explain both.
teaching.audioText: A strong correlation does not demonstrate that one thing causes another, because a third factor may explain both.

teaching.en: Because the sleep hours were self-reported, the authors cannot rule out that some pupils exaggerated, so the figures may be biased.
teaching.es: Como las horas de sueño eran autodeclaradas, los autores no pueden descartar que algunos alumnos exageraran, así que las cifras pueden estar sesgadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Rule out + that + oración significa «descartar»; biased indica que el método inclina el resultado.
segments: Because the sleep hours were self-reported, the authors cannot rule out
that some pupils exaggerated, so the figures may be biased.
teaching.audioText: Because the sleep hours were self-reported, the authors cannot rule out that some pupils exaggerated, so the figures may be biased.

teaching.en: A key limitation is that only one school took part, so the conclusions may not be justified beyond it.
teaching.es: Una limitación clave es que solo participó una escuela, así que las conclusiones pueden no estar justificadas fuera de ella.
teaching.explanationEs: Justified aplicado a una conclusión indica que los datos la sostienen; beyond it = más allá de esa escuela.
segments: A key limitation is that only one school took part,
so the conclusions may not be justified beyond it.
teaching.audioText: A key limitation is that only one school took part, so the conclusions may not be justified beyond it.

teaching.en: Even a large sample cannot warrant a sweeping claim when no comparison group exists, since other causes remain possible.
teaching.es: Ni siquiera una muestra grande puede justificar una afirmación demasiado general si no hay grupo de comparación, pues otras causas siguen siendo posibles.
teaching.explanationEs: Warrant + afirmación = justificarla; un sweeping claim abarca más de lo que los datos pueden respaldar.
segments: Even a large sample cannot warrant a sweeping claim when
no comparison group exists, since other causes remain possible.
teaching.audioText: Even a large sample cannot warrant a sweeping claim when no comparison group exists, since other causes remain possible.

teaching.en: Headlines often overstate a claim that the researchers made cautiously, and robust evidence is rarely as tidy as the headline suggests.
teaching.es: Los titulares suelen exagerar una afirmación que los investigadores hicieron con cautela, y las pruebas sólidas rara vez son tan limpias como sugiere el titular.
teaching.explanationEs: Overstate a claim = presentarla más fuerte de lo que los datos permiten; robust evidence exige muestra amplia y comparación.
segments: Headlines often overstate a claim that the researchers made cautiously, and
robust evidence is rarely as tidy as the headline suggests.
teaching.audioText: Headlines often overstate a claim that the researchers made cautiously, and robust evidence is rarely as tidy as the headline suggests.

prompt.es: Elige el verbo que mantiene la afirmación dentro de lo que muestran los datos.

choices.text: proves
guarantees
suggests

feedback.es: Sin grupo de comparación y con voluntarios, el verbo adecuado es cauto: suggests; proves y guarantees prometen más de lo que hay.

hint.es: Piensa qué verbo deja abierta la posibilidad de otras causas.

origin.text: The trial had no comparison group, and the results held only for volunteers. The authors write: This study ___ that light exercise may help people to sleep.

prompt.es: Completa: «La correlación no demuestra que una cosa cause la otra.»

feedback.es: Dos datos que suben juntos muestran una correlation; un tercer factor (el calor) puede explicar ambos.

hint.es: Sustantivo que significa que dos datos van juntos sin que uno cause el otro.

origin.text: Ice-cream sales and beach visits rise together, but the ___ between them does not demonstrate that one causes the other; the hot weather explains both.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de una reseña con el problema que revela.

pairs: All the volunteers came from one firm.
Workers described their own habits.
Nobody was followed over several years.
The paper names a third factor.

feedback.es: Cada frase señala un tipo distinto de límite: muestra, origen del dato, falta de seguimiento o causa alternativa.

hint.es: Pregúntate qué no puede afirmarse a partir de cada frase.

pairs: All the volunteers came from one firm.
Workers described their own habits.
Nobody was followed over several years.
The paper names a third factor.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué significa que el resultado sea «tentative, not conclusive».

choices.text: It hints at a possible benefit without settling whether the desks cause it.
It means the desks do reduce pain, although nobody has measured how much.
It shows that the survey was carried out carelessly.

feedback.es: Tentative indica una pista provisional; not conclusive, que no zanja la cuestión: los escritorios pudieron comprarse precisamente donde ya había dolor, así que no se sabe si reducen el dolor ni cuánto.

origin.audio: The authors of a large survey found that people who use standing desks report less back pain. However, the desks were bought by companies that had already noticed staff complaints, so the people with desks may have been the ones in pain to begin with. The authors therefore call their result tentative, not conclusive.

prompt.es: ¿Qué conclusión está justificada por este ensayo?

choices.text: The tablet improved sleep, as the comparison with the group that took nothing shows.

answer.text: Our survey of two hundred pupils produced two main findings. First, sixty per cent of the pupils sleep less than eight hours a night. Second, among those who sleep little, twice as many girls as boys say that they feel tired in class. These figures suggest that a lack of sleep may affect how pupils feel at school, and they appear to show that girls are more affected than boys, at least to some extent. However, the results have an important limitation. All the pupils came from one school, and they described their own sleep, so the data may not be reliable. For this reason, we cannot say that sleep causes tiredness; we can only say that the two seem to be linked. Further research with a larger sample from several schools would be needed before anyone could generalise these results to all teenagers. We therefore treat them as a starting point, not as proof. In short, the findings stand out and deserve attention, but they should be read with caution.

We asked two hundred pupils about their sleep and found two things that stand out. To begin with, 60 per cent of them sleep for less than eight hours a night. In addition, among the pupils who sleep little, double the number of girls compared with boys reported feeling tired during lessons. The data indicate that a lack of sleep could affect how pupils feel at school, and girls seem to be more affected than boys to some extent. Nevertheless, there is a key limitation: only one school took part, and the pupils reported their own hours, so the answers may not be reliable. Because of this, the results do not show that sleep causes tiredness; they only point to a link. Further research with a larger sample from different schools would help us to see whether the same pattern appears elsewhere, and whether anyone can generalise from it. We therefore see them as a starting point, not as proof. To sum up, the findings are useful, but they must be treated with caution.

answer.text: Last June a survey was conducted among three hundred residents of the old neighbourhood. The participants were selected at random from a list and were asked to complete a questionnaire online. Two results stand out. First, roughly a third of the residents said that the street lighting is poor, whereas the vast majority praised the park. Second, twice as many older residents as young ones feel unsafe at night. These findings suggest that lighting may be a top priority for the neighbourhood, and they appear to show that older people are more worried. However, there is an important limitation: most answers came from two streets, and the residents described their own feelings, so the data may be biased. For that reason, we cannot generalise the results to the whole city. As a next step, we propose a three-month trial run of new lamps in the two streets, and we suggest that the council should report the results in the autumn. Further research with a larger sample would then show whether the change really helped, and whether residents in other streets feel the same way.
accepted: Last June a survey was conducted among three hundred residents of the old neighbourhood. The participants were selected at random from a list and were asked to complete a questionnaire online. Two results stand out. First, roughly a third of the residents said that the street lighting is poor, whereas the vast majority praised the park. Second, twice as many older residents as young ones feel unsafe at night. These findings suggest that lighting may be a top priority for the neighbourhood, and they appear to show that older people are more worried. However, there is an important limitation: most answers came from two streets, and the residents described their own feelings, so the data may be biased. For that reason, we cannot generalise the results to the whole city. As a next step, we propose a three-month trial run of new lamps in the two streets, and we suggest that the council should report the results in the autumn. We conducted a survey in June, and three hundred residents of the old town answered an online questionnaire. They were chosen at random from a local list. We found two main things. To begin with, about a third of the residents think the street lighting is poor, while the vast majority like the park. In addition, double the number of older people compared with young people feel unsafe when they walk at night. This indicates that better lighting could be a top priority, and it seems that older residents are more concerned. Nevertheless, there is a limitation. Most of the answers came from two streets, and people only reported how they feel, so the results may not be reliable. We therefore cannot say that the same is true for the whole city. Our proposal is a trial run of three months with new lamps in those streets, and we recommend that the council reports the results in the autumn. More research with a larger sample would show whether the trial helped and whether people in other streets feel the same.

Límite: respondieron sobre todo vecinos de dos calles y los datos son declarados. Propuesta: una prueba de tres meses con farolas nuevas y un informe del municipio. Escribe unas 180–280 palabras en inglés.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende lograr la carta al admitir que las respuestas vinieron de dos calles?

choices.text: To apologise for a survey that the residents no longer believe in.
To be open about the limits so that the request sounds more credible.
To suggest that the lighting is a problem only in those two streets.

feedback.es: Reconocer el límite con franqueza da credibilidad a la petición; no pretende eximirse de pruebas ni insinúa desacuerdo del resto.

origin.text: Dear Councillor, I write on behalf of the residents of Mill Lane. Our survey, completed by two hundred and forty neighbours, found that nearly a third consider the street lighting poor, whereas most are satisfied with the park. We accept that the answers came mainly from two streets, and we do not claim to speak for the whole neighbourhood. Nevertheless, twice as many residents over sixty as under thirty told us that they no longer walk home after dark. We ask the council to consider a trial run of brighter lamps in our street, and we would be glad to help to monitor the results.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los vecinos pueden plantear dudas sobre si la muestra los representa.»

feedback.es: Raise concerns (o voice/express concerns) es la colocación para plantear dudas de forma explícita.

origin.text: The sample came mainly from two streets. Residents elsewhere may well ___ concerns about whether it speaks for them, and the authors should answer those concerns openly.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué temor expresa uno de los vecinos.

choices.text: That three months is too short to show whether the lamps help.
That the lamps will cost more than the council has said.
That a trial could be used to put off the decision.

feedback.es: El vecino advierte de que una prueba piloto pueda servir de excusa para retrasar la decisión; el sobrecoste lo menciona la funcionaria, no el vecino, y el plazo de tres meses no se cuestiona.

origin.audio: At the next meeting, the council's officer admitted that the survey had been well run but said that the lamps would cost more than expected. She proposed starting with one street and reporting back in three months, so that members could weigh up the results before spending any more. Several residents welcomed the idea, though one warned that a trial might be used as an excuse to delay a decision.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito defiende el autor una prueba piloto?

choices.text: To gather evidence of the effect before committing money.
To protect the council from blame if the lamps prove unpopular.
To prove that the survey's percentages were exaggerated.

feedback.es: Defiende la prueba para obtener pruebas del efecto antes de gastar; no habla de proteger al municipio y reconoce que los vecinos pueden tener razón, así que no refuta las cifras.

origin.text: A survey can tell a council what people say they feel, not what will work. Residents who ask for brighter lamps may well be right; even so, a trial run would show whether fear falls, and that is a better reason to spend public money than a percentage.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los vecinos pueden plantear dudas, pero el plan parece viable.»

answer.text: Residents may raise concerns but the plan seems feasible

feedback.es: May raise concerns admite la duda legítima y but the plan seems feasible la contrarresta.

prompt.es: Completa: «La mayoría elogió el parque, mientras que un tercio criticó el alumbrado.»

feedback.es: Whereas contrasta dos datos de la misma encuesta y va precedido de coma.

origin.text: The vast majority praised the park, ___ roughly a third were unhappy with the street lighting, so the council has a clear priority.
